brief: Goldman notes a divergence between AI/semis price action and levered-ETF flows. The SOX index posted its worst week of the year (-11%), second worst since Liberation Day, and SMH fell for 9 straight sessions, the longest losing streak in its 15-year history; SPY, XLK and QQQ outperformed SMH for 10 straight sessions despite composition overlap. Despite this weakness, nearly $10bn flowed into levered ETFs last week, the largest weekly inflow in GS's dataset, led by SOXL (+$7bn, a record, 74% of inflows) and TQQQ (+$1.3bn). GS frames this as consistent with a historical pattern: levered-ETF flows are strongest on days of sharp market declines (-2σ) and weakest on the best days (+2σ), and larger in absolute size during steep selloffs. The week's inflows pushed cumulative YTD levered-ETF flows toward net-positive, which GS is watching because improving market conditions could amplify gross levered exposure (currently $152bn AUM, $386bn gross, the second-lowest since July).
